subject: Roadmap: MAP close - provisioning & network bind for CardioIQ POC
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Li <samantha@cardioiq.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 Aug 2025 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Roadmap: MAP close - provisioning & network bind for CardioIQ POC

Hi Samantha / Raj,

Thanks again for the demo last week — excited about CardioIQ moving forward with the evaluation. Per our MAP discussion, attached is a condensed list of provisioning steps we need to complete to hit the close date (target: 2025-08-28). High level:

- Org & admin setup: Redwood will create the POC tenant; we need a CardioIQ admin user to accept invite.
- API keys: we will provision an ephemeral API key for the trial and a production-scoped key upon activation.
- IP allowlist: provide the public IP ranges for your firewall.
- VPC peering (optional): if you want private connectivity we can initiate peering; requires account IDs + CIDR overlap check.

Action items for CardioIQ (please reply inline):
1) Confirm admin email for org invite.
2) Share the IP ranges we should allow (or confirm you want peering instead).
3) Any procurement constraints (PO terms, required ML/data handling addenda)?

I've attached a lightweight network diagram and a one-page MAP action tracker for the POC. Neha and Jonas are on copy for the network/VPC details — they will own the peering/IPS configuration and the key lifecycle.

If it helps, I can open a short 30-min checkpoint on Thursday to walk through the config checklist and commit timelines.

—Markus
Markus Klein
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
(attachment: cardioiq-network-diagram.pdf)

From: Samantha Li <samantha@cardioiq.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@cardioiq.com>, procurement@cardioiq.com
Date: Tue, 12 Aug 2025 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Roadmap: MAP close - provisioning & network bind for CardioIQ POC

Thanks Markus — this looks good. Quick answers inline:

1) Admin for invite: raj.patel@cardioiq.com (Raj will own the onboarding).
2) IP allowlist: initial perimeter will be our web tier public IPs: 34.210.112.0/24 and 52.14.200.128/26 (we can expand later). We are open to peering but need to confirm with infra.
3) Procurement: we need standard PO (Net 45) and a signed DPA (we'll send our standard redlines). Also would like a SOC2 summary before we kick off any data access.

Could you attach the MAP tracker as a Google Sheet and share edit access? Raj and procurement want to see the timeline.

-Samantha
Samantha Li
Head of Product, CardioIQ

Great — thanks for the quick answers, Raj/Samantha. Next steps and clarifications:

- I invited Raj to the POC org (invite pending acceptance).
- IPs noted (34.210.112.0/24, 52.14.200.128/26). If you prefer peering instead, we'll need your AWS/VPC account ID and the VPC CIDR so we can run an automatic overlap check.
- Procurement: attaching a one-page SOC2 summary for now; our security team will follow up with the full report under NDA if required.
- MAP tracker: shared as Google Sheet (link below) with the live action items. We'll also export an XLSX and attach for your procurement team if helpful.

Immediate technical ask for your infra team (Neha copied):
1) Confirm whether you want the ephemeral API key only (public allowlist) or peering+private keys. Ephemeral key turnaround is ~1 hour after we have the admin accepted.
2) If allowlist: confirm a single outbound port range is acceptable (443 + 12000-12002 for health probes).
3) If peering: provide VPC account ID and CIDR by EOD Friday 2025-08-15 so we can create the peering request and fill the MAP milestone.

Links:
- MAP tracker (view/edit): https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1AbCdeMAPTracker
- HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.redwood/deals/DEAL-1784
- DocuSign (procurement): https://docusign.com/aa/authorize/3xF2fQ

Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf, map-action-items.xlsx

I'll schedule a 30-min checkpoint for Thursday 2025-08-14 10:00 PT; if that doesn't work we can shift.

—Markus
(attachment: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf, map-action-items.xlsx)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Samantha Li <samantha@cardioiq.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@cardioiq.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 14 Aug 2025 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Roadmap: MAP close - provisioning & network bind for CardioIQ POC

Looping in the network ops specifics before the call. Quick technical notes (for CardioIQ infra):

- Public allowlist option: we will provision an ephemeral TLS-scoped API key. Traffic will come from the following egress ranges (Redwood-hosted): 52.233.48.0/22, 18.197.16.0/21. Please add those to your firewall along with the two ranges you provided.
- Port requirements: All traffic over HTTPS (443). We also use an internal health probe range 12000-12002 if you plan to inspect deep packet. Those probes originate from the egress ranges above.
- Peering option: Provide AWS account ID and the VPC CIDR (example: 10.10.0.0/16). We do not accept overlapping CIDRs. Peering also requires an IAM role ARN for route propagation automation (Neha will provide exact role template).
- Key lifecycle & rotation: ephemeral POC key TTL = 72 hours. For production keys we require an owner (CardioIQ admin) to approve rotation cadence in the MAP sheet.

I'll attach the JSON template for the peering request in the shared drive during the call and post the role ARN template afterward.

See you on the checkpoint — Markus, could you convert the map-action-items to an editable tab named "Network" before the call?

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
(attachment: peering-request-template.json)
notes: Call scheduled: Thu 2025-08-14 10:00 PT. Procurement indicated Net 45 + DPA redlines; DocuSign link provided.
